purpose: the Memory Covenant's semantics as original machine-checkable formulas — the math behind the standards wedge

authority.note: candidates only; promotion to the locked reference requires Lean-proven carriers, exactly like F1-F22

candidates.name: deny-by-default-safety
candidates.statement: For a memory M with admission set A (the reviewed facts), a decision function d that reads only from A cannot be influenced by any fact outside A: for all unadmitted f, d(M) = d(M \union {f}). Injection is structurally impossible.
candidates.wedge_use: the IETF answer: governed memory provably admits no unreviewed influence
candidates.expected_proof: filtering argument: d factors through the admission projection; unadmitted facts are in the kernel
candidates.status: CANDIDATE — to be proven in Lean when the Mathlib build completes

candidates.name: staleness-propagation
candidates.statement: If source s is stale at time t, then every result r derived from s is stale at t, and the staleness label is preserved under every derivation in the estate's composition rules. A stale record cannot become fresh by derivation.
candidates.wedge_use: staleness that cannot be laundered — formalized

candidates.name: learning-monotonicity
candidates.statement: The admitted-knowledge set is monotone non-decreasing across review cycles, and no unreviewed candidate enters it: admitted(c+1) >= admitted(c), and x in admitted(c+1) implies x was reviewed before cycle c+1.
candidates.wedge_use: the 'agent that tried to remember something it wasn't allowed to' demo, as a theorem

candidates.name: confabulation-floor
candidates.statement: CONJECTURE: for the tested model family (0.8B-4B), there exists a fabrication rate floor on unanswerable probes that is invariant under fine-tuning across the three tested curricula. Five receipted measurements support it; no proof is claimed.
candidates.wedge_use: the honest flagship: a conjecture labeled as a conjecture, with the evidence on the chain
